[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/02/18 (Sat) 19:28  
[USER] The user has been experiencing some digestive issues lately.  
[USER] The user is wondering about probiotics and how they can help with gut health.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Probiotics are live microorganisms (bacteria or yeast) that help maintain a healthy balance of gut flora.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Probiotics can be found in fermented foods like yogurt, kefir, sauerkraut, kimchi, and kombucha, or taken as dietary supplements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Probiotics help maintain a healthy balance of gut flora, improve digestion, boost the immune system, reduce inflammation, and produce vitamins.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Probiotics can alleviate digestive issues such as bloating, gas, diarrhea, constipation, IBS, and IBD.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] When selecting a probiotic supplement, consider strain, CFU count (at least 1 billion CFU per serving), delivery form, storage, and third-party testing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The user should consult with a healthcare professional before starting any new supplement.  
[USER] The user asks for the recommended daily intake of probiotics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The recommended daily intake of probiotics varies:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] General health and wellness: 1-10 billion CFU (International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics) or 1-2 billion CFU (National Institutes of Health).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For IBS: 1-10 billion CFU per day, with some studies suggesting up to 20 billion CFU for severe symptoms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For IBD: 1-10 billion CFU per day, with some studies suggesting up to 50 billion CFU for severe symptoms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For immune system support: 1-5 billion CFU per day, with some studies suggesting up to 10 billion CFU.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For digestive health: 1-5 billion CFU per day, with some studies suggesting up to 10 billion CFU for severe issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Age-specific recommendations: Infants (0-12 months): 100 million to 1 billion CFU; Children (1-12 years): 1-5 billion CFU; Adults: 1-10 billion CFU; Pregnant or breastfeeding women: 1-5 billion CFU.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The quality of the probiotic supplement is more important than the quantity.
